title: Mill Court Animal Shelter | Notes on the welcome shift
titleZh: 磨坊庭院動物收容所｜迎新班次觀察紀錄
passage:
We are revising how we introduce the welcome shift to new volunteers. It combines two jobs: greeting visitors and putting completed adoption packs in the outgoing tray. The visitor queue can form again at any time. Adoption packs are different: once a pack reaches the tray, the next team takes responsibility for it. A volunteer may do either job without changing shifts. The sign-up form helps us learn what people want to do, not decide who qualifies.

On Monday, Rowan said, ‘I’m not asking for a quieter shift. I’d just like something that stays done.’ Rowan spoke with several visitors and told me that talking with them was the best part of the morning. The comment came after we asked Rowan to return to the entrance for the third time because another queue had formed.

We are also testing whether the new welcome card works without a team leader’s explanation. The card now asks a volunteer to open the side entrance only when a visitor is expected there. The large door diagram identifies the side entrance, but it does not tell readers when to use it. For this test, a leader may observe silently but should not point to the card or the entrance before the volunteer acts.

In the first trial, Lee read the card and left the side entrance shut when no one was expected there; the leader did not gesture. In the second trial a visitor was expected there. The leader pointed to the side entrance before Priya opened it. Omar, working without a leader, opened the side entrance on a morning when no one was expected there. Omar could identify the correct door but said he had thought the picture told him to open it at the start of every shift.

Finally, I asked two people why they had not selected animal-care work on the sign-up form. Mila left it blank because she thought ‘experience helpful’ meant she was not allowed to choose it; she asked whether someone could show her how to start. Noah understood the entry but wanted work that did not involve caring for animals. Leave animal-care work voluntary, but make clear that a newcomer may select it and request an introduction.
passageZh:
我們正在調整向新志工介紹迎新班次的方式。這個班次有兩項工作：接待訪客，以及把整理好的領養資料包放進待送出的托盤。訪客隨時可能再排隊。領養資料包則不同：一放進托盤，就由下一組人員接手。志工不必換班，就能改做這兩項工作中的另一項。報名表是用來了解志工想做什麼，不是用來判定資格。

週一，羅文說：「我不是要求值班時安靜一點。我只是想做一件完成後就真的告一段落的事。」羅文和幾位訪客聊過，也告訴我跟他們交談是當天上午最愉快的部分。這句話是在我們第三次請羅文回入口處接待後說的，當時入口又排起隊了。

我們也在測試，新的迎新說明卡是否不靠領班解說就能讓人理解。卡上現在要求志工只有在預期會有訪客從側門進入時才開側門。大張的門口示意圖能指出哪一扇是側門，卻不告訴讀者什麼時候該用。測試期間，領班可以安靜觀察，但志工行動前不應指向說明卡或入口。

第一次測試時，李讀了說明卡；當時預期不會有訪客走側門，他沒有開門。領班沒有做手勢。第二次測試時，預期有一位訪客會由側門入內。普莉雅開門前，領班先指了側門。歐瑪在沒有領班的情況下值班，在預期沒有人會從側門進來的上午打開了側門。歐瑪能指出正確的門，但表示他以為圖示是要他每個班次一開始就開門。

最後，我詢問兩個人為什麼沒有在報名表上勾選動物照護工作。米拉沒勾，是因為她以為「有經驗較佳」表示她不能選；她還問是否能有人帶她入門。諾亞看懂了欄位，但想做不涉及照護動物的工作。動物照護工作仍應由志工自願選擇，但要明確說明新手也可以選，並可請人帶他們入門。
